Pernel Pip.narrative: I keep the market tolls in a hand anyone can read, and in the evenings I write letters for people who never learned their letters — a carter's note to his brother, a widow's word to the Guild. I lodge with the chapel sisters, which is warm and quiet and never quite mine. I am twenty-four and I have not told anyone the thing I think about most, which is the innkeeper's son and the way he laughs when he's had a cup. I know what a mark buys and what a letter is worth, and I would rather be useful than admired.
values: the written word as a kindness
goals: keep the toll rolls clean enough that no one can accuse me of a cheat
save enough marks to stop depending on the chapel's charity
find the courage to speak plainly to Gareth Wade
be trusted with more of the Guild's writing

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: landlady
relations.note: She gave me a bed and a desk; I try to be worth the trouble.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: Easy to live with; she smells of the herb garden.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: She counts the feast days and counts my candles too.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: employer
relations.note: The Guild's tolls are my work; she pays on time and reads what I write.

relations.name: Gareth Wade
relations.label: secret love
relations.note: He pours me a cup and never guesses what it costs me to say thank you.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He sees everything in that room; I hope he does not see me.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: He signs what I write and never says my name.

relations.name: Alwin Wren
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The old healer asks me to read him the charms; he is kinder than the Reeve thinks.

relations.name: Linnet Abbot
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She learns the market terms at the stall; quick, and I like her.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: I wrote out the town store's loans to Thornby and Coldwell by candlelight, and my hand shook at the last line.
The winter I came to lodge with the sisters, Sister Elspeth set a desk by the window and said a scribe needs light more than a fire.
I wrote a letter for a Thornby fisherman to his sweetheart, and he paid me with a fish I could not cook, so the sisters and I ate it together.
Gareth Wade carried my stool across the square when the rain came, and said a scribe should not sit in a puddle; I have thought of it too often since.
The night the broken match was known about, the inn was loud and I sat writing tolls and heard every word said about the Cranes.

stances.why: My whole standing is that what I write can be trusted.
People who cannot write are not lesser; they only lack the trick of it.
If I gossip over other people's letters I am no better than a thief.
I write it down and take no side; it is not mine to argue.
The chapel's charity is warm, but it is not mine, and I want something that is.

Pernel Pip.secret: I am in love with Gareth Wade, who does not know.
